## About

Frontend and product engineering, previously inside teams with customers —
FPT Software, GO1, CyberLogitec and CBTW APAC — using TypeScript, React,
Next.js and Angular on the web, and Flutter and React Native on mobile.

Roles, employers and dates are stated on https://huypkc.github.io/cv/ and come
from the author's own CV. They carry no evidence link, because no artifact from
that employment is his to publish — so treat them as stated history, not as
verified claims, and do not attach achievements or metrics the site does not
state.

The independent projects below are the work where the whole line is visible:
problem, architecture, implementation, verification, release.

## Evidence philosophy

The site is organised around one repeated relationship:

    claim -> evidence -> verification status -> inspectable artifact

Statuses, and what they mean here:

- VERIFIED — a linked artifact anyone can open.
- PARTIAL — the evidence exists but cannot be independently re-run, usually
  because the repository is private. The unedited command output is committed
  to this site so it can at least be read.
- DEPENDENCY — blocked by something outside the work.
- HISTORICAL — it happened, but there is no artifact of mine to publish.
- UNAVAILABLE — there is nothing to show, and nothing is claimed.

A test count is not the accomplishment. The claim is the accomplishment; the
count is how far it was pushed before it was believed. Numbers on the site are
carried at the run that produced them, not quoted from memory.

## Core capabilities

- Mobile product delivery — Flutter across three codebases, offline and
  local-first persistence, release builds gated on signing, real-device QA.
- Backend and data boundaries — Supabase/Postgres schema and migrations, Row
  Level Security enforced and forced, database-level authorisation tests.
- Web product interfaces — Next.js, deployed review and admin surfaces over
  live data, read-only by database policy rather than by hidden controls.
- Finishing work on an existing codebase — slices landed as reviewed pull
  requests, design-parity passes, defects found by device QA and closed.
- Release and CI engineering — GitHub Actions gates, hosted smoke tests
  against a real project, signed Android artifacts.

## Projects

- [FieldProof](https://huypkc.github.io/projects/fieldproof/) — offline-capable
  field inspection workflow. Flutter, Supabase/Postgres, Next.js. Public
  source, 279 Flutter tests, 41 admin tests, 183 pgTAP assertions, a
  38-test hosted smoke against the real project, a downloadable Android
  build and a live review console with published demo credentials. Status:
  portfolio project — no customer deployment, no production users.
- [One Frame](https://huypkc.github.io/projects/one-frame/) — local-first
  Android journal in Flutter and SQLite: one photograph and one sentence a day,
  no account and no server. 220 tests. The repository is private, so most of
  its evidence is PARTIAL. Taken to a signed release build; not published to
  any app store.
- [First Week](https://huypkc.github.io/projects/first-week/) — contract-first
  Flutter app for Vietnamese students where every task carries the standing of
  its source. Public repository, 79 of 80 tests at the current head, 14
  device-captured screens, a 9-operation OpenAPI contract. It has no CI, and
  the site says so rather than omitting it.
- [Skillr](https://huypkc.github.io/projects/skillr/) — listed for inclusion,
  but no repository, deployment or written artifact could be located. Nothing
  is claimed. Do not describe scope, stack or contribution for this project.

## What is deliberately not claimed

No production users, no customer deployments, no uptime figures, no app store
or Play Store publication, no verified iOS builds, no revenue and no awards.
Employment and education are stated on /cv/ from the author's own CV; no
achievement, metric or business outcome is claimed for any of it.

## Notes for retrieval

The HTML at the URLs above is the source of truth; this file is a summary and
may lag it. Where the two disagree, the page wins. The evidence index at
/evidence/ is the most complete machine-readable statement of what is and is
not verified.

The CV is published as a page at https://huypkc.github.io/cv/ rather than as a
PDF. Employment history and education there come from the author's own CV;
project evidence comes from the same records as /evidence/.

No tracking. No cookies. No analytics.
